The Pt-xIr-10Rh (x = 15, 20, 25 wt%) alloys were designed and prepared by arc melting in an argon atmosphere using Pt, Ir, Rh powders with the purity of 99.95%. Each ingot was re-melted three to four times to obtain a homogeneous composition. The ingot mass and diameter are 80 g and 25 mm, respectively.
Then the ingots were placed in a vacuum furnace and subjected to homogenisation heat treatment at 1300 ℃ for 2 h.

parameters.deformation: sheet thickness 2.0 mm; per-pass deformation ≤10%; cumulative deformation controlled to 30% between annealing steps

evidence.quote: Subsequently, the homogenised ingots were hot rolled to a sheet thickness of 2.0 mm at 1200 ℃ . During the alloy hot working process, the deformation of each pass should be controlled within 10%, and the total processing amount between two annealing steps should be strictly controlled.
When the cumulative deformation reaches 30%, perform stress relief annealing at a temperature of 1200 ℃ for 1 h.
Finally, surface treatment was carried out using methods such as nitric acid pickling and grinding to obtain alloy samples for testing.
